module.name: Awareness Function (AWX)
module.description: Defines Awareness as a dynamic, systemically differentiated condition for converting potential utility into effective utility. Awareness connects visceral, emotional, and cognitive processes and determines whether behavior becomes utility-effective at the moment of decision (Moment of Truth). The definition follows Meta-Axiomatics MA_0.00 l-r and z-zc.

A1.title: Definition - Function, Systematics and Meta-Embedding of the Awareness Function
A1.text: Awareness is the necessary condition for potential utility (individual, collective, identity-based) to be converted into effective utility at the Moment of Truth. Awareness encompasses the consciousness of one's own impact - positive or negative - on individual, collective, and identity-based utility types. It includes physiological (SYS 0), affective-emotional (SYS 1), and cognitive-reflective (SYS 2) system levels. The core formula is: U_eff,X(t*) = U_pot,X(t*) × A_SYSi,X(t*), where X ∈ {INU, KNU, IDN} and i ∈ {0,1,2}. Systemic levels include: SYS0 (Instant) - automatic visceral activation without conscious processing; SYS1 (Affective) - emotional awareness of meaning and social resonance; SYS2 (Reflective) - cognitive awareness of effect, consequence and meaning in context of rules and norms.

A2.title: Scope & Context - Range, Situational Conditions and Systemic Connection
A2.text: Describes the functional range of Awareness across utility types (INU, KNU, IDN), contexts, and decision situations. Awareness (A_SYS0-2) operates exclusively situationally at the Moment of Truth and mediates between potential and effective utility. The functional scope rule states: Awareness only operates when at least one utility type is active at the Moment of Truth. Context integration sources include modules 8904_KON, 9492_KOM_META, 9485_UNS_ENV, 9493_UNS_INS, 9495_UNS_IPN, and 9494_UNS_EPI. The Moment of Truth (t*) is the decision point where potential utility can be transformed into behavior through awareness. Cross-module links connect upstream to utility modules (7234_INU, 7235_KNU, 7236_IDN) and downstream to willingness (7243_WAX), probability (7259_PRB), and journey (7256_JNY).

A3.title: Objectives - Goal, Function and Direction of the Awareness Function
A3.text: Defines the functional objectives of the Awareness function within BCM. Core objectives include: O1 - Transformation of potential into effective utility (U_eff,X(t*) = U_pot,X(t*) × A_SYSi,X(t*)); O2 - Reduction of knowledge-action gap (Δ(Action-Knowledge) ∝ 1/A_total); O3 - Integration of external effects on others; O4 - Systemic differentiation connecting three system levels (visceral, affective, reflective); O5 - Enabling compliance and honesty through reflective self-assessment; O6 - Maintaining meta-coherence (Σ|ΔA_SYSi| ≤ θ_meta); O7 - Feedback-based learning capability (A_SYS2(t+1) = A_SYS2(t) + ρ_feedback × ΔOutcome_impact); O8 - Strengthening collective decision quality. Awareness functions as a multiplicative amplifier and filter between utility modules and willingness.

A4.title: Axiomatics - Fundamental System Rules
A4.text: Complete axiom system organized in 8 clusters covering fundamental transformation rules, determinants, utility-type specificity, complexity and uncertainty effects, temporal dynamics, conflict and dissonance, segmentation logic, and interaction patterns.

axioms.title: Awareness Transformation Condition
axioms.description: Potential utility becomes effective only when Awareness > 0 at moment t*. Awareness functions as a multiplier and filter between utility potential and behavior. Exception: Instant INU (physiologically immediately perceptible) and Instant IDN (socially-emotionally immediately perceptible) automatically activate with A=1. KNU (collective utility) always requires awareness.

axioms.title: Community Relevance
axioms.description: Awareness is the consciousness that one's own behavior has effects on the utility of a relevant community.

axioms.title: Social External Effects
axioms.description: Awareness is only behavior-effective when effects on collective or identity-based utility of a relevant community are recognized.

axioms.title: Time-Delayed Individual Utility
axioms.formula: A_mod(t) > 0 ⇒ N_ind(t+h) salient when h > θ_instant
axioms.description: Awareness also includes individual utility with delayed effect that must be made anticipatorily salient.

axioms.title: Moment of Truth
axioms.description: Awareness operates exclusively at the moment of decision. Only context-specific trigger-activated awareness is effective.

axioms.title: Situational Activation
axioms.description: Only awareness activated by context-specific triggers is effective.

axioms.title: General Awareness as Learning Effect
axioms.description: General awareness emerges exclusively through repeated situational activation.

axioms.title: Dynamic Salience
axioms.description: Awareness changes depending on the temporal dynamics of the perceived context.

axioms.title: Positive and Negative Impact
axioms.description: Awareness mandatorily encompasses both positive and negative effects of behavior.

axioms.title: Instant Utility Exceptions
axioms.formula: If X ∈ {INU_instant, IDN_instant} → A_X(t*) = 1; if X = KNU → awareness required
axioms.description: Certain utility effects occur instantly without awareness (INU_instant, IDN_instant). Collective utility is never instant.

axioms.title: General vs. Situational
axioms.description: Only situational impact awareness at the Moment of Truth is behavior-effective.

axioms.title: Interindividual Differences
axioms.description: Awareness level varies between individuals due to cognitive, emotional, social, and biological factors.

axioms.title: Cognitive Structuring Ability
axioms.description: Whether awareness is reflected depends on literacy, media competence, and logical modeling ability.

axioms.title: Context Dependency
axioms.description: Awareness is completely context-bound.

axioms.title: Context as Amplifier or Blocker
axioms.description: Context factors can amplify or block awareness.

axioms.title: Limitation
axioms.description: Awareness is limited by attention capacity.

axioms.title: Uncertainty and Ambiguity
axioms.description: Ambiguity, risk, and uncertainty slow down or distort awareness learning.

axioms.title: Salience and Priming
axioms.description: Awareness emerges only when utility is salient or activated through priming.

axioms.title: Hyper-Awareness
axioms.formula: A_mod(t) ≫ A_norm(t) ⇒ ∀N_x(t) salient, even when Relevance(N_x) ≈ 0
axioms.description: Awareness can be exaggerated so that even minimally relevant utilities become salient.

axioms.title: Awareness Blockade
axioms.formula: A_mod(t) = 0 ⇒ N_x(t) not salient despite Relevance(N_x) > 0
axioms.description: Awareness can be blocked so that relevant utilities do not become salient.

axioms.title: Habitualization
axioms.description: Habitualized behavior patterns do not require awareness.

axioms.title: Decay Effect
axioms.description: With increasing habitualization, functional access to awareness decreases.

axioms.title: Clinical Relevance
axioms.description: Persistent deviations (hyper or blockade) become clinically relevant when distress or function loss occurs.

axioms.title: Cognitive Attention Span
axioms.description: Awareness level increases with available attention and decreases with overload.

axioms.title: Cognitive Load
axioms.description: Awareness decreases with increasing cognitive load from parallel tasks or information.

axioms.title: Evidence Availability
axioms.description: Awareness increases with clarity, simplicity, and visibility of evidence for impact.

axioms.title: Availability Heuristic
axioms.description: Awareness increases with mental availability of examples or memories.

axioms.title: Emotional Valence
axioms.description: Positive or negative affects increase awareness for associated utility.

axioms.title: Fear as Amplifier
axioms.description: Fear particularly strongly increases awareness for negative impact.

axioms.title: Hope as Amplifier
axioms.description: Hope increases awareness for positive impact.

axioms.title: Affective Resonance
axioms.description: Awareness increases when behavior is linked with strong emotional reactions.

axioms.title: Social Norm Pressure
axioms.description: Awareness increases when behavior is strongly socially sanctioned or rewarded.

axioms.title: Social Mirroring
axioms.description: Awareness increases when behavior is visibly mirrored by peers or relevant others.

axioms.title: Network Effects
axioms.description: Awareness increases when behavior is amplified visible in social networks.

axioms.title: Institutional Legitimacy
axioms.description: Awareness increases when behavior is supported by institutions perceived as legitimate.

axioms.title: Institutional Trust
axioms.description: Lack of trust in institutions lowers awareness level.

axioms.title: Rule Clarity
axioms.description: The clearer rules are, the higher awareness for their impact.

axioms.title: Cultural Narratives
axioms.description: Awareness increases when behavior is embedded in existing narratives.

axioms.title: Symbols & Rituals
axioms.description: Cultural symbols and rituals particularly strongly increase awareness level.

axioms.title: Priming Effects
axioms.description: Conscious or unconscious priming increases the probability that utility becomes salient.

axioms.title: Biological Factors
axioms.description: Awareness varies with biological characteristics such as age, gender, neurodiversity.

axioms.title: Energetic State
axioms.description: Awareness decreases with exhaustion and increases with high energy.

axioms.title: Interactive Determinants
axioms.description: Awareness results from the interaction of multiple determinants (e.g., emotion × norm pressure).

axioms.title: Awareness INU
axioms.description: Awareness for individual utility means consciousness that one's own behavior has positive or negative influence on one's own individual utility.

axioms.title: Awareness KNU
axioms.description: Awareness for collective utility means consciousness that one's own behavior has positive or negative influence on the utility of a community or group.

axioms.title: Awareness IDN
axioms.description: Awareness for identity utility means consciousness that one's own behavior has positive or negative influence on belonging, recognition, or identity.

axioms.title: Utility Type Differentiation
axioms.description: Awareness is differently pronounced depending on utility type: INU is strongest, KNU weakest, IDN strongly context-dependent.

axioms.title: Instant INU
axioms.description: Physiologically perceptible individual utility effects (e.g., hunger, pain, fatigue, dopamine kick) are instant and require no awareness.

axioms.title: Instant IDN
axioms.description: Emotionally-socially perceptible identity utility effects (e.g., applause, shame, symbols) are instant and require no awareness.

axioms.title: No Instant KNU
axioms.formula: For all U_pot,KNU: A_KNU(t*) < 1 when no awareness
axioms.description: Collective utility is never instant. All KNU effects require awareness.

axioms.title: Interaction INU ↔ KNU
axioms.description: Awareness for KNU increases when an INU is simultaneously affected.

axioms.title: Interaction INU ↔ IDN
axioms.description: Awareness for INU increases when behavior simultaneously has identity relevance.

axioms.title: Interaction KNU ↔ IDN
axioms.description: Awareness for KNU increases when belonging to a community is strongly salient in terms of identity.

axioms.title: Awareness Hierarchy
axioms.description: In conflict cases, awareness INU dominates over IDN and IDN over KNU.

axioms.title: Awareness Overlay
axioms.description: Awareness for one utility type can temporarily overlay awareness for another.

axioms.title: Awareness Multiplication
axioms.description: Total effective utility results as sum of awareness-filtered utility types.

axioms.title: Awareness Sensitivity
axioms.description: Awareness threshold differs by utility type: INU has low threshold, KNU high threshold.

axioms.title: Awareness Amplification through Multiple Effects
axioms.description: When behavior simultaneously affects INU, KNU and IDN, awareness increases multiplicatively.

axioms.title: Complexity Reduction
axioms.description: Awareness decreases with increasing complexity of the decision situation.

axioms.title: Necessity of Framing
axioms.description: At high complexity, awareness is only possible through simplification, framing, or heuristics.

axioms.title: Failure Awareness Gap
axioms.description: Awareness is systematically distorted when failures remain communicatively, institutionally, or culturally invisible. The Failure Awareness Gap describes the collective perception gap that emerges when errors are socially stigmatized, not reported, or algorithmically filtered out.

axioms.title: Environmental Uncertainty
axioms.description: When consequences of behavior in the environment are uncertain, awareness level decreases.

axioms.title: Interpersonal Uncertainty
axioms.description: Awareness decreases when it is unclear how other individuals will react.

axioms.title: Institutional Uncertainty
axioms.description: When trust in institutions is lacking or rules are unclear, awareness decreases.

axioms.title: Epistemic Uncertainty
axioms.description: When knowledge about cause-effect relationships is missing, awareness falls to zero.

axioms.title: Uncertainty Accumulation
axioms.description: Awareness decreases more strongly when multiple uncertainty types occur simultaneously.

axioms.title: Uncertainty Differentiation
axioms.description: Awareness reacts differently strongly to various uncertainty types: epistemic > institutional > interpersonal > environmental.

axioms.title: Complexity-Uncertainty Interaction
axioms.description: Complexity amplifies the effect of uncertainty and reduces awareness disproportionately.

axioms.title: Necessity of Institutional Aids
axioms.formula: If Complexity & Uncertainty high → A_X(t*) = f(Institutional_Aid)
axioms.description: At high complexity and uncertainty, awareness can only be secured through institutional orientation aids (e.g., rules, standards, labels).

axioms.title: Situativity
axioms.description: Awareness exists only in specific situations and contexts. It is not permanent.

axioms.title: Fluctuation
axioms.description: Awareness level fluctuates strongly over time depending on context and person factors.

axioms.title: Decay Effect
axioms.description: Awareness decreases exponentially without renewed triggers.

axioms.title: Reactivation
axioms.description: Awareness can be reactivated or amplified through repeated triggers.

axioms.title: Habitual Attenuation
axioms.formula: A_X(t*) → 0 with high repetition without variation
axioms.description: Repeated exposure can weaken awareness when a stimulus becomes routine.

axioms.title: Life Phase Dependency
axioms.description: Awareness level varies systematically across life phases (childhood, adolescence, adulthood, old age).

axioms.title: Life Events
axioms.description: Certain critical events (e.g., birth, death, illness, job loss) abruptly change awareness.

axioms.title: Shock Trigger
axioms.description: Sudden shock events massively and immediately increase awareness.

axioms.title: Long-term Stabilization
axioms.description: Repeated confrontation with stimuli can stabilize awareness long-term if they remain variable and salient.

axioms.title: Journey Integration
axioms.description: Awareness acts as trigger in specific phases of the Behavioral Change Journey.

axioms.title: Suppression
axioms.formula: If Awareness → negative Emotion strong → A_X(t*) ↓
axioms.description: Awareness can be consciously or unconsciously suppressed when it is unpleasant or threatening to the individual.

axioms.title: Cognitive vs. Emotional Split
axioms.description: Individuals can be cognitively informed about an impact without emotional awareness emerging.

axioms.title: Norm Conflict Blockade
axioms.description: Awareness can be blocked when different social norms send contradictory behavioral signals.

axioms.title: False Awareness
axioms.description: Misinformation, propaganda, or distorted frames can create consciousness that is factually false.

axioms.title: Collective Overlay
axioms.description: Collective narratives or group identities can overlay or suppress individual awareness.

axioms.title: Mirror Coherence and Awareness Dissonance
axioms.formula: A_X(t*) = f(MirrorGap_t); ∂A_X/∂ΔI_t > 0 for ΔI_t < 0.6; ∂A_X/∂ΔI_t < 0 for ΔI_t ≥ 0.6
axioms.description: Awareness reacts to the difference between self-image and social feedback, measured as Mirror-Gap. Small differences promote learning-awareness, large differences activate protective-awareness.

axioms.title: Segment Dependency
axioms.description: Awareness level varies systematically between segments defined in module 7257.

axioms.title: Player Types
axioms.description: Awareness level differs by player type (e.g., Cooperative, Competitive, Strategic) according to module 9479.

axioms.title: Cultural Differentiation
axioms.description: Awareness level varies strongly between cultures due to different narratives, symbols, and institutions.

axioms.title: Education and Competence Level
axioms.description: Awareness level increases with higher education and competence level, decreases with low knowledge.

axioms.title: Socioeconomic Status
axioms.description: Awareness level depends on socioeconomic status: resource wealth enables higher awareness.

axioms.title: Aggregation of Individual Awareness
axioms.description: Collective awareness level results from aggregation of individual awareness values within a group.

axioms.title: Dynamic Multiplicity
axioms.formula: A_Group(t*) = Σ w_i * A_i(t*), w_i ≠ constant
axioms.description: Aggregated awareness level is not linear but determined by dynamic weights (e.g., influence of individual actors).

axioms.title: Awareness Cascades
axioms.description: An awareness expression or action can trigger a cascade that increases awareness in other individuals.

axioms.title: Awareness Spillover
axioms.description: Awareness in one area can amplify or activate awareness in other areas.

axioms.title: Awareness Blockades
axioms.description: Toxic communication (e.g., hate speech, targeted disinformation) can block awareness at the collective level.

A5.title: Requirements - Entry Conditions and Determinants
A5.text: Defines the structural, contextual, and psychological prerequisites under which Awareness can become effective at the Moment of Truth. Requirements include: R1 - Utility basis (INU, KNU, IDN must be fully defined); R2 - Impact relations (mapping between behavior and utility must be known); R3 - Determinants across cognitive, emotional, social, institutional, cultural, biological, communicative dimensions; R4 - Time context (Moment of Truth must be contextualized and defined); R5 - Instant exceptions (INU_instant and IDN_instant operate without awareness; KNU always requires awareness); R6 - Segmentation (awareness varies by segment logic); R7 - Communicative dynamics (collective awareness influenced by Overconfidence, Survivorship Bias, Failure Gap); R8 - Thresholds (ΔAwareness_F > 0.25 triggers Perceptual Lock-In and automatic Watchdog activation).

A6.title: Integration - Systemic Connection with Other BCM Modules
A6.text: Defines the logical, functional, and governance interfaces between the Awareness function and other core BCM 2.0 modules. Awareness functions as an intermediary transformation variable between utility, context, uncertainty, complexity, and willingness. Upstream modules include utility types (7234_INU, 7235_KNU, 7236_IDN), context logic (8904_KON), complexity (9492_KOM_META), uncertainty modules (9493-9495), player types (9479), game theory (9480), watchdog (9251), statistics (9477), and meta-axioms (7232_META). Downstream modules include willingness (7243_WAX), probability function (7259_WTX), decision probability (7260_PRB), segment logic (7257_SEG), behavioral change journey (7256_JNY), and life phase logic (7457_LCP). In version v5.0, communicative biases (Bias Block: Overconfidence, Survivorship Bias, Failure Gap) are integrated with watchdog trigger AWX_FailureGap_Alert when ΔAwareness_F > 0.25.

A7.title: Boundaries - Delimitation from Related Concepts
A7.text: Defines what Awareness is NOT within the BCM 2.0 framework. With version v5.0, boundaries against systemic, communicative, and bias-based pseudo-awareness states are added. Awareness exclusively denotes real-time cognitive, emotional, or reflective processing of one's own utility impact at the Moment of Truth - independent of socially mediated frames, discourses, or perception biases. Awareness ≠ Knowledge (information can exist without consciousness); Awareness ≠ Attitude (preferential but not real-time behavior-relevant); Awareness ≠ Motivation (motivation can exist without impact awareness); Awareness ≠ Information (communication ≠ consciousness of consequences); Awareness ≠ automatic processes (exception: Instant INU or IDN); Awareness ≠ norm enforcement (conformity can occur without consciousness); Awareness ≠ strategic rationality (planning ≠ impact consciousness); Awareness ≠ stable trait (it is dynamic and context-dependent); Awareness ≠ utility itself (it mediates but does not create utility); Awareness ≠ complete behavior control (it is necessary but not sufficient condition); Awareness ≠ visibility (public communication ≠ individual consciousness); Awareness ≠ transparency (transparency can exist without being perceived); Awareness ≠ feedback (feedback creates awareness only when internalized); Awareness ≠ discourse (social debates do not create individual awareness per se); Awareness ≠ data awareness (algorithmic presentation does not replace consciousness of impact); Awareness ≠ false awareness (misinterpretations or framing create pseudo-consciousness).

A8.title: Use Cases - Application Areas
A8.text: Practical application areas include: Simulation of knowledge-action gaps; Modeling of biases (e.g., loss aversion); Design of interventions (priming, framing, defaults); Segment and target group analysis; Journey mapping; Life phase analysis; Uncertainty and complexity analysis; Strategic simulation (player types, game theory); Monitoring and control (Watchdog, hate speech); Empirical measurement (statistics).

A9.title: Limitations - Constraints and Boundaries
A9.text: Inherent limitations include: Limited attention span; Selectivity and bias; Strong context dependency; Fluctuation and decay over time; Lack of sustainability; No guarantee for behavior; Measurement problems; Manipulability; Weakness with collective utility; Awareness is only a multiplier, not a complete explanation.

A10.title: License & Governance - Control Architecture and Ethical Use
A10.text: Regulates the use, control, and governance of the Awareness function within BCM 2.0. Version v5.0 introduces automatic monitoring of communicative biases (Overconfidence, Survivorship Bias, Failure Gap) through Watchdog module 9251, ensuring perceptual integrity of Awareness in real-time. Ownership: FehrAdvice & Partners AG; License type: BCM 2.0 Core License; Mandatory status: Core module - no valid simulation or intervention architecture without Awareness. Usage rules: R1 - Exclusive use within licensed BCM models; R2 - All extensions must be axiomatically consistent and meta-validated; R3 - Errors or uncontrolled bias amplifications trigger automatic Watchdog checks; R4 - All applications must be disclosed and documented (governance protocol requirement); R5 - Covert influence or manipulative use excluded; R6 - Goal is promotion of fair, transparent, and adaptive decision architectures. Bias monitoring automatically tracks Bias_total = Bias_conf + Bias_surv + Bias_fail + κ(Bias_conf × Bias_surv × Bias_fail) with Watchdog triggers when ΔAwareness_F > 0.25 or κ > 0.10. Ethics: E1 - No psychologically or socially harmful effects; E2 - Applications must aim at awareness promotion, not distortion; E3 - Module serves collective orientation, fairness, and decision quality; E4 - Users and organizations bear full responsibility for integrity, transparency, and traceability.
